chapter_title: The Chapter of the Man who asks: Why [am] I sometimes at peace, and troubled at other times?
chapter_note: The chapter is a dialogue: a heavy frame/question section (¶1–5) including experiential self-report and a clearly institutional/pious vignette (¶4), followed by a compact cosmological-mechanistic answer about the Light Mind, astrological disturbance, and the mixed character of nourishment (¶6–11). No NT-citation overlay appears; the main late material is the hagiographic/dialogue apparatus and recap-style address to the disciple.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic dialogue opening (“Once again… I beseech you, my master”), a classic Kephalaia frame marker.
First-person experiential report within the question scene; not systematic cosmological exposition but part of the dialogue setup.
Extended first-person complaint/psychological turbulence in Q&A mode (application/affect language), functioning as the disciple’s question material rather than an impersonal cosmological mechanism.
Institutional piety vocabulary (fasting, praying, reciting psalms) and brother-relations; this is church-practice coloration rather than cosmos→cosmos mechanism.
Petition/transition back to the master (“So now I beseech you…”), serving as scene management.

paragraphs.core_text: The soul that assumes the body, when the Light Mind will come to it, shall be purified by the power of wisdom and obedience, and it is cleansed and made a new man. There is no trouble in (the soul), nor confusion nor disturbance.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution and approval formula: “Then the apostle speaks thus to the disciple: Well do you ask… Behold, I will explain it to you! ⟨p.215⟩ Understand this:” as compilation-frame speech.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core cosmological mechanism (Light Mind purifying the soul) embedded in explicit dialogue-frame/authorial staging (“apostle… to the disciple”).

paragraphs.core_text: However, when a disturbance will arise for him and he will be troubled, this disturbance shall go into him in [ ... ], first through his birth-signs and his difficult stars that [ ... ] they turn over him and stir him and trouble him with lust and anger and depression and grief, as he wills. Also, as he wills, the powers of heaven shall trouble him through their roots, to which he is attached.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal causal explanation inside the cosmic system (birth-signs, difficult stars, powers of heaven, roots/attachments) rather than institutional application.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, there are times you shall find the powers of heaven are peaceful and tranquil for him, and it comes to [ ... ] a difficult part comes into him by the nourishment that he has eaten, or else indeed in some [ ... ] or in the water that they have drunk. Again, trouble and confusion and anger will increase in him, and lust multiplies upon him together with depression and grief; because of the nourishment of the bread he has eaten and the water he has drunk, which are full of bothersome parts, a vengeful counsel. They shall enter his body, [mixed in] with these foods, and they even become joined in with the wicked parts of the body and the sin that is in him; transferring the anger and the lust and the depression and the grief, these wicked thoughts of the body.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic-physical mechanism: disturbances mediated through mixed nourishment and bodily ‘parts’; still cosmos/anthropos mechanics rather than exhortation or church practice.
Recap/bridging in second-person with explicit ‘I have explained to you’ meta-discourse; functions as editorial/compilation connective, and is too lacunose to securely isolate substrate wording.

paragraphs.core_text: There are times, however, if you shall find that the nourishment that comes into you is pure [ ... ... ], so it is greater in light and life while the waste is less in it, and the evil-doing is diminished from it. Even the atmosphere above is still, being purified through the [ ... ... ] also the image is calmed from [ ... ... ] increases in you through ⟨p.216⟩ those good parts of the food that come into you. And they find you at ease and tranquil, as you are well governed in your abodes because of the living part, which is greater on account of the light of these justified souls that are in it. The ones that have perfected their deeds. Their dues have ceased, while their soul is carefree [ ... ] they have been allied with these living souls that [are p]resent in you. Due to this you shall find them in you, calm in tranquillity, and they come from you without trouble; and you are found flourishing of body. Even your deeds are determined, being well constructed after their manner, and your doctrines are in order, as your words [ ... ] your soul is carefree within you, ascending like a bird.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Extended internal mechanism (purity of nourishment ↔ light/life balance ↔ justified souls present within the mixture), with correspondential imagery (soul ‘ascending like a bird’) but no turn to institutional/polemical targets.

paragraphs.core_text: when [your bo]dy is troubled, you shall be troubled by the conduits of they below, the difficult parts that come into you by food and the act of eating. Again, when the conduits above are calmed from you, even your food that has come into you is clear and pure. Your heart shall be found ordered in its place, your counsels at peace from disturbance.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed recap and first-person explanation scaffolding: “Behold, I have explained to you… I have told you that…” which is compilation-style address rather than the mechanism itself.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Contains a clear core causal scheme (conduits below/above; food-mediated influx) embedded in a concluding ‘I explained’ discourse typical of the compiled Q&A presentation.
Formulaic closing praise of the apostle and blessing language; hagiographic/community frame.
